prs.body:
Visitors now use one restaurant/fry search with address, radius, style, price and rating filters. Regular users submit businesses for review; administrators publish stores, review requests and authorize other admins. Optional profile addresses remain private.

Implements FRY-45 through FRY-56 with additive database upgrades, Google Places (New) integration, accessible debounced address suggestions, explicit device-location controls, an idempotent Kenosha place-ID importer, and Flask-WTF signed CSRF protection. Updates Requirements and setup documentation; relocates Sprint 2 reports and demo into docs/sprints/sprint-2.

Validation: 48 passing isolated integration/regression tests, including forged/cross-client/session-rotation CSRF checks; JavaScript syntax validation; desktop and 390px mobile search inspection with no horizontal overflow; missing-key fallback verified in browser.

Final automated analysis at b93baae14b9fefb54077c02bad7f740cb358902b: SonarQube Community Build 26.10.0.133078 reports 0 bugs, 0 vulnerabilities, 0 code smells, 0 security hotspots and Quality Gate PASS. Trivy 0.76.0 filesystem/dependency scan reports 0 CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW vulnerabilities. Initial findings were fixed and rescanned without suppressions. Later commits only add report/evidence files.

Reports: [Jira report](https://github.com/JoeBeebz/RateMyFries/blob/feature/sprint-3-discovery-and-business-moderation/docs/sprints/sprint-3/Sprint-3-Jira-Report.md), [GitHub report](https://github.com/JoeBeebz/RateMyFries/blob/feature/sprint-3-discovery-and-business-moderation/docs/sprints/sprint-3/Sprint-3-GitHub-Report_Seth-Martin.md), [static-analysis PDFs and raw evidence](https://github.com/JoeBeebz/RateMyFries/tree/feature/sprint-3-discovery-and-business-moderation/docs/sprints/sprint-3/static-analysis). All submissions are committed through this PR.

Acceptance limits: Google Cloud project/key/billing are not configured. Live Google autocomplete/geocoding and actual Kenosha import remain unverified; no real Google businesses or fabricated menus/ratings were added. A trusted operator initializes the first admin once; subsequent admin authorization requires an existing admin.

Required approving review is still pending. Jira records 8 stories In Review and 4 Google-dependent stories In Progress, with 0 Done. The active sprint and merged-only GitHub report do not misrepresent unmerged work as delivered.

prs.body:
The class site at its LAN HTTP address throws `crypto.randomUUID is not a function` while initializing address suggestions. That also prevents the current-location handler from registering. Generate UUIDv4 session tokens with `crypto.getRandomValues` when `randomUUID` is unavailable, and preserve each address input's accessible name while suggestion/loading text changes.

Tracks [FRY-56](https://ratemyfries.atlassian.net/browse/FRY-56) and the affected control in [FRY-46](https://ratemyfries.atlassian.net/browse/FRY-46). Adds four Node regression checks covering HTTP/HTTPS token generation, keyboard selection, token rotation/independence, and unavailable/denied location fallback. Documents the Jira-first and teammate-review workflow.

Validation: existing Python suite 48 passed; four new JavaScript checks passed; JavaScript syntax and whitespace checks passed. An isolated server preview returned live Google suggestions, accepted ArrowDown/Enter selection, and reported no browser errors. Google address lookup, autocomplete and five operational Kenosha businesses were verified from the deployment server with a Places-only, server-IP-restricted key. The already-merged importer was activated separately and a repeat import retained identical counts without inventing menus or reviews.

The class test release at `d094cd8e52b1dcf413ed1a36209a367abe525262` now includes this fix alongside PR #9 and quality PR #10. Existing class users, restaurant/fry data, reviews and signing key were preserved, with database/application backups and the prior release retained. Live LAN HTTP Google suggestions and ArrowDown/Enter selection passed. This is a test deployment; teammate approval and merge are still required for Jira Done. Device geolocation still needs a browser-trusted origin and a working device location provider; address-entry fallback remains available.

prs.body:
The class directory had five imported Google locations and no fry products. Add a curated catalogue with ten additional Kenosha/Pleasant Prairie restaurants, enrich four existing listings, and provide 37 published fry options, 14 restaurant/brand photos and 20 matching product photos.

Tracks [FRY-57](https://ratemyfries.atlassian.net/browse/FRY-57), created before implementation. Full menu, location and photo source URLs plus verification dates are recorded in the manifest; visitor-facing descriptions contain only the food/restaurant description, as requested for the class project. Source records stay in the manifest. Photos identify brand/menu imagery. No prices, ratings or reviews are invented, and no restricted Google content is cached. Tr3s Hermanos and the existing owned placeholder are preserved without speculative menus/photos.

The standalone operator utility previews by default, requires a private backup directory for writes, matches durable place IDs or normalized names/addresses, fills blank metadata and inserts missing fry names. Owned/ambiguous conflicts roll back the transaction. It preserves existing human edits and review IDs on repeat imports.

Validation: 54 Python tests passed; all 29 distinct image URLs served image content; isolated live-database copy added exactly ten restaurants and 37 products, and a repeat run added nothing. The same content is now loaded into the live database after a consistent backup. Existing accounts, reviews, business requests and the owned placeholder were verified unchanged, database integrity/foreign keys passed, and the existing application source/release remains unchanged. Live restaurant pages show the photos and fry menus; a captured live page was checked at 390 px with the clean visitor-facing descriptions.

This PR contains the reproducible content manifest, operator utility, tests and documentation. It does not change runtime application code or schema. Do not merge without teammate approval; FRY-57 remains In Review until approval/merge and acceptance checks are complete.

prs.body:
Search currently accepts arbitrary partial text without helping visitors choose a listed entry. Add catalogue autofill to the homepage and discovery form, with pointer and Arrow Up/Down + Enter selection. Only existing public restaurant/fry names and available styles whose names START WITH the typed text are suggested. Sort matches alphabetically and cap the combined dropdown at six options total; each extra letter narrows the list. The behavior is generic, with no business names hard-coded. Names load once per page and are filtered locally, separately from Google address autocomplete.

Enforce complete listed names/styles on the server while preserving case/whitespace normalization and the existing filters. `Wingstop` returns the restaurant and all its fries; `wngstop` and unselected partial names return zero results. Blank input still browses the catalogue. No pending submissions/private addresses enter the suggestion list, and source values render as text.

Tracks [FRY-58](https://ratemyfries.atlassian.net/browse/FRY-58), created before implementation. Validation: 61 Python tests and four Node interaction checks passed, JavaScript syntax passed, and whitespace checks preserve existing tracked CRLF endings. A private preview using the populated database verified keyboard and pointer selection, Wingstop = one restaurant/four fries, wngstop = zero/zero, and readable suggestions at 390 px. Prefix checks verified W = six options, Wa = four, Waf = three, and We = Wendy's; a fixture with more than six matching entries verifies the total cap. See docs/search-autofill.md.

At the user's explicit request, commit `be7e01b` is now deployed to the existing class server for testing. The old release is preserved and private application/SQLite backups were created before the atomic release switch. Accounts, 16 restaurant listings and 37 fry products stayed unchanged; database integrity/foreign keys passed. Live browser checks show six W suggestions; live search returns one Wingstop/four fries and zero typo matches.

This test deployment does not merge the PR. Teammate approval, merge and user/live acceptance remain required for Jira Done. The separate description cleanup is live and its utility update remains in PR #8; Google address initialization is independently tracked by PR #7.

prs.body:
Restaurant discovery took 2–3.5 seconds because live Google business lookups ran sequentially. A shared eight-worker pool now fetches them concurrently, preserving ordering and fetching fresh details on each request. The class-dataset preview measured a 402ms median and 1,288ms maximum over five searches, below Seth's approved 2-second response target (FRY-44).

FRY-40 changes improve rating/control contrast, narrow-screen wrapping and search loading feedback. FRY-46 changes explain the LAN HTTP location limitation and prevent late GPS callbacks from overwriting a newly selected address.

Validation: 49 Python tests and 8 JavaScript checks pass on this branch; an isolated combination with PR #9 passed 62 Python tests and 12 JavaScript checks. Edge 156.0.4314.58 rendered 17 pages at 390px and 1280px with no horizontal overflow in 34 layouts; 31 shared-palette contrast checks pass. Live preview registration, profile/address suggestions, saved-address discovery, catalogue selection and review submission passed. Raw measurements and reproducible layout/contrast tools are included in [the acceptance report](docs/quality/acceptance-2026-11-03.md).

This PR is stacked on **PR #7** and targets its feature branch to keep the quality diff separate. Merge #7 only after teammate approval, then retarget this PR to `main`; reconcile and rerun tests with #9 before this PR's approved merge. No main merge or self-approval has occurred. FRY-40/44 remain In Review pending team acceptance/merge; other browser engines are not separately verified. FRY-46 remains In Progress: the explicitly authorized real device request returned no position, fallback worked, and actual GPS acceptance still needs a trusted origin/device.

Class test release is deployed at `d094cd8e52b1dcf413ed1a36209a367abe525262`, combining the pending #7/#9/#10 runtime changes without merging main. Backup and prior release are preserved; class users, 16 restaurants, 37 fries and review data were unchanged. Post-deployment LAN response checks (three runs) measured search at 488/353/311ms, home at 21/15/16ms, restaurant details at 181/187/186ms and fry details at 28/25/16ms.

prs.body:
Copy the existing Fry development server to private EC2 while preserving the personal-server website and database. The deployed t4g.micro uses an encrypted disk, stable outbound address and zero inbound security-group rules. The app listens on loopback and is viewed through authenticated Session Manager forwarding. The instance is stopped between work sessions and was left stopped after acceptance.

Two parameterized identities receive complete Linux administration plus connection/start/stop/reboot access to this instance. IAM/billing administration, instance deletion and unrelated resource changes are excluded. AWS-generated temporary console passwords require first-sign-in reset; collaborator names and credentials are outside Git/Jira. Each person completes their own sign-in and password choice. A separate Places-only key is restricted to the new outbound address; the original server configuration is unchanged.

Includes a reproducible CloudFormation template, bootstrap, encrypted-transfer restore with runtime/import/HTTP checks, Windows connection helper and cost/backup/rollback guide. Secrets do not enter Git, Jira or SSM command text. The migrated source is the actual deployed revision d094cd8, including earlier feature work still pending its own PR reviews; this PR does not merge or replace those reviews.

Validation: 52 repository tests passed, Python compilation, PowerShell parsing and whitespace checks passed, and AWS CloudFormation completed successfully. Live acceptance verified SQLite integrity/foreign keys, 1 existing account, 16 restaurants and 37 fry listings; private homepage/search/details, exact-name search and misspelling rejection, six autocomplete options and loaded photos, restricted Google city lookup, both Linux sudo paths, and 13 allowed/denied IAM cases per identity. Public ports 22/80/443/8000 were unreachable. An authenticated tunnel displayed the website; actual reboot automatically restored a 200 homepage. The original personal service remained active. Base estimate: $10.42/month continuously running or $4.29 stopped, before tax/transfer/Google usage; keep compute stopped when idle.

[FRY-59](https://ratemyfries.atlassian.net/browse/FRY-59) is In Review. Remaining acceptance: individual first sign-ins/password changes and teammate PR approval/merge under the repository workflow. No unapproved main merge was performed.
